My son started last September and is thriving! I have been very impressed with his progress and he's always very keen to get to school - he loves it!
The school works in partnership with parents and are highly inclusive of children with additional needs. The staff see the individual child and their potential. We are grateful that CJS have gone above and beyond to ensure that our child has an appropriate level of support.
Moving to Clanfield has been the best decision we have made and we can actually relax knowing our children are safe and we don't have to worry.
My child is happy and progressing because he has a teacher who values him and his personality. She understands him and how to make him thrive.
Clanfield has been the best school we have encountered. The staff are lovely. Our child is excelling better than in any other year and is very excited to learn. Wonderful environment! Thank you!
Everyone is included at Clanfield Junior School. In particular, pupils with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) feel welcomed, supported and cared for by staff and pupils alike. One pupil noted, ‘It’s good that we are all different, it would be boring if we were all the same.’
​​​​​​​A Message from our Headteacher
Welcome to Clanfield Junior School – a place where every child is encouraged to be the best that they can be!
I am incredibly proud to be the Headteacher of Clanfield Junior School; a warm, inclusive and vibrant school where our children are truly at the heart of everything we do. We have worked hard to create a strong identity as a school family, where everyone is welcome, everyone brings value, and every child is known, loved and nurtured. Our school values – Be Kind, Be Resilient, Be Respectful and Be Curious – underpin everything we do. They encourage children to aim high, enjoy learning and feel proud of who they are and what they achieve.

Inclusion - Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
At Clanfield Junior School we embed inclusivity throughout our teaching and school culture. We cultivate an atmosphere where diversity is celebrated and every child has the opportunity to achieve their full potential, developing both academically and personally. Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEN) provision is designed to ensure all children have equitable access to a rich educational experience.
We have an Inclusion leader (Mrs Pinhorne) who is our ambassador for children with SEND needs, vulnerable groups and children who are disadvantaged.
Our core values ‘Be kind, Be respectful, Be resilient and Be curious’ are at the heart of our SEN provision, creating an enriching, supportive environment where every student can succeed, feel part of a caring school community and ‘Be the best that you can be!’
If you have any concerns about your child's progress, please make an appointment with your child's class teacher in the first instance to discuss any support they might benefit from.
Our Inclusion leader is Mrs Katie Pinhorne. She can be reached via email at [email protected].
Please read our Inclusion Information Report and SEND Policy (see links below) for additional information on our approach to supporting the needs of children with SEND, in line with the Department for Education Special Educational Needs and Disability Code of Practice, 0-25 years (2015).

PE and Sport Premium
The PE and Sports funding is a government scheme which is designed to help primary schools improve the quality of PE and sports activities they offer to children in schools. As a Junior School, we receive funding for Years 3 – 6. We take great pride in our sporting offer and have used our sports funding effectively in 2024-2025 to result in being awarded the Gold Sports mark. Our children have taken part in a huge range of enrichment activities- see our sporting opportunities page for some of our examples.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clanfield Junior School - Parents and Carers
pageCache.text:
Parents and Carers
We warmly welcome our parents and carers to our school and website. We want families to feel informed, involved and confident in what we do, and this section has been designed especially with you in mind. Here, you’ll find everything you need in one easy place — including information about after-school clubs, wrap-around care, uniform, school timings and all those helpful day-to-day details.
Parent voice and a strong partnership with families are incredibly important to us. We regularly involve parents in shaping the direction of the school, and we are proud of how much of our practice has been influenced by your ideas. Recent examples include the outdoor nature cabin, updates to our school uniform and day timings, our new anti-bullying policy, feedback surveys and much more. We love receiving suggestions, as they often spark exciting new opportunities — such as the creation of our Allergy Ambassadors after parents highlighted the importance of being an allergy-aware school.
We also encourage you to enjoy our school newsletters, which offer a lovely snapshot of life at CJS and are always filled with updates, celebrations and upcoming events.

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Children playing with a parachute
Our Vision
For every child to feel safe, happy and grow both personally and academically through the strong relationships within our school community and beyond.
Our Vision is what we strive to achieve as a school community, and it is at the heart of what we do.
Children listening to RNLI demonstration.
Children creating a design together for a project.
Children solving a science problem together.
Our curriculum aims:
Our Values
Our School Values were chosen and agreed upon by our wonderful children, their families, and our dedicated staff team in the summer of 2023. They are incredibly important to us, as they define what it means to be part of Clanfield Junior School and guide everything we do.
We live and breathe our values every day — through whole-school and class assemblies, volunteering roles, school trips, our curriculum, and through the way we treat and support one another.
Children are recognised and celebrated for showing our values in action. They can earn special value wristbands and have the opportunity to be nominated for the weekly Class Star Award, which shines a light on those who go above and beyond in demonstrating what it means to be a true member of the Clanfield community. Our values are more than just words — they are the foundation of who we are and the reason our school continues to be such a kind, caring, and inspiring place to learn.
2 friends smiling together
Class of children smiling
Child out in the snow
Be Kind – Be Resilient – Be Respectful – Be Curious
‘Be the Best that You Can Be.’

Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium at Clanfield Junior School
The Pupil Premium Grant is additional government funding given to schools to help ensure that every child has the same opportunities to succeed, regardless of their background or personal circumstances.
At Clanfield Junior School, we use this funding carefully to remove barriers to learning and provide the right support for every child to be the best they can be. This might include:
Providing extra academic support and small-group teaching.
Offering extra emotional or wellbeing support
Helping with access to trips, clubs or enrichment opportunities.
Developing resources and training to support high-quality teaching for all.
We review how the funding is used each year to make sure it is having a positive impact on children’s progress, confidence and enjoyment of school life.
You can read more in our Pupil Premium Strategy Statement, which outlines our current priorities and how we measure success.

After school clubs
We are delighted to offer a wide range of after-school clubs, run by both our dedicated staff and specialist external providers. There truly is something for everyone — from football, art and gardening to coding and other exciting opportunities to learn new skills. Our aim is to make sure there is something for everyone. Have a look at the external links on the right of this page too!
How do we select our clubs?
At Clanfield Junior School, we listen carefully to our pupils. Pupil voice plays a big part in shaping our club provision and ensuring every child feels included and inspired. By analysing club uptake data and gathering pupil feedback, we have been able to adapt our offer to better reflect the interests and passions of our children.
As a result, our club offer includes a fresh mix of new CJS staff-led clubs and externally run activities delivered by experienced sports coaches. We continue to monitor participation and feedback closely so we can shape an even stronger term by term offer that meets the needs of all our pupils.
All children get a chance to request a space instead of 'first come, first served', and then we carefully make sure that everyone gets a club.

Personal Development
Personal Development and SMSC at Clanfield Junior School
At Clanfield Junior School, we prioritise helping every child grow into a kind, confident, and responsible individual who is ready to make a positive difference in the world. Belonging is at the heart of our school and this drives our plans- we are continually looking for new ideas that bring us even more together as a school family. We have a huge range of outdoor provision for our children- take a look at The Great Outdoors to find out more.
Our assemblies are an integral part of our week- make sure you have a look at this on our website! We also have a new page celebrating our exceptional children who go above and beyond, showing kindness and courage to make a positive difference to either our school, our community, or even the wider world.
We are fiercely proud of the wide range of opportunities we provide for our children and are always planning new ideas and enrichment events to help every child thrive. We protect childhood, promote diversity, and support children in understanding the important role they play within the community. One example is when our children met the the ‘Tallest Professional Basketball Player in the World.’ Paul shared how he embraced his visible difference and used it to his advantage.
Pupil voice (check out our school councillors ) is central to our approach, enabling children to contribute meaningfully and make positive changes in the right way. We have been learning about the British values that shape our country and why they are important in helping us live together respectfully and responsibly.
Our approach to Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural (SMSC) development is woven throughout school life. It shapes our curriculum, assemblies, behaviour expectations, and the many wider opportunities our children experience each day. Read our newsletters to see the huge range of weekly events that take place!
Here are a few examples:
Spiritual Development
We encourage pupils to reflect, ask big questions, and develop a sense of curiosity about the world around them. Through lessons, assemblies, and experiences in nature, children are given opportunities to explore feelings of awe, wonder, and empathy. They learn to appreciate their own beliefs and values while respecting those of others.

Religious Education
Religious Education at Clanfield Junior School
At Clanfield Junior School, Religious Education (RE) is taught in line with national legal requirements. Our curriculum reflects that the religious traditions of Great Britain are primarily Christian, while also exploring the teachings and practices of other principal religions represented in our country. We have very strong links with our local Church and the wonderful Rev Anne Gothard.
We aim to create a learning environment where children show respect, tolerance, and open-mindedness towards people of all faiths and beliefs.
Through RE, pupils are encouraged to be curious, ask thoughtful questions about the world, and develop a deeper understanding of their own beliefs, values, and experiences. This approach supports the development of key British Values, including mutual respect, individual liberty, and tolerance of those with different faiths and world views.

Pupils at Clanfield Junior School learn about Christianity, Islam and Judaism. They also complete an overview study of Buddhism in Year 5 and Year 6. At least two of the four ‘golden thread’ concepts (love, special, belonging and community) are taught each year, a continuation of their Infant School curriculum. These help to broaden and deepen the pupils’ understanding of religious education throughout KS1, KS2 and KS3.
Each unit of learning begins with a ‘hook’ to support the pupils with their understanding of the concept and immerse them in the learning. Much of the RE teaching is carried out through exploring the children’s ideas and emphasis is given to positive, high quality discussion. Pupils also complete written outcomes, express their views through pieces of arts and scrutinise scripture. There are opportunities throughout the curriculum for visiting experts, trips to local places of worship and virtual visits, which further enhance the learning experience.
Religious Education at Clanfield Junior School will develop pupils into considerate members of the community who are able to respect and appreciate other faiths, beliefs and cultures. By the end of KS2, pupils at Clanfield Junior School will be able to explain how the key concepts that they have been taught can be applied to their own lives and the lives of others and be ready to continue their learning in KS3.
Right to Withdraw from Religious Education (RE)
Parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE). If you are considering this, we encourage you to speak with the school first. This allows us to explain what is taught, answer any questions, and support you in making an informed decision.
If you decide to withdraw your child, a formal request must be made in writing to the Headteacher. Please see the document below for further information.
Finding Out More About Our RE Curriculum
We believe it is important for parents, carers, and members of the community to understand what we teach and why. You can find information about our RE curriculum by:
Visiting the Curriculum section of our school website
Contacting the school office to request a copy of our RE curriculum overview
Speaking directly with your child’s class teacher or the RE Subject Lead
Requesting a meeting if you would like to explore the curriculum in more detail
We welcome questions and are happy to provide any further information you may need.
